items.label: section_header
items.text: KEY POINT

items.label: text
items.text: Methyl orange is red in acidic solutions and yellow in alkaline ones. However, when it is used as an indicator in titrations (see Chapter 16) involving adding an acid to an alkali, an orange colour is usually obtained, which indicates the endpoint. Orange is a mixture of the red and yellow forms.

items.label: text
items.text: Carbonates react with dilute acids in the cold, and so does magnesium. Most other things that you are likely to come across need to be heated.

items.label: section_header
items.text: MAKING SODIUM, POTASSIUM AND AMMONIUM SALTS

items.label: text
items.text: In the method we've just been looking at, you add an excess of a solid to an acid, and then filter off the unreacted solid. You do this to make sure all the acid is used up. This method does not work for making sodium, potassium and ammonium salts.

items.label: text
items.text: The problem is that all sodium, potassium and ammonium compounds are soluble in water. The solid you added to the acid would not only react with the acid, but any excess would just dissolve in the water present. You wouldn't have any visible excess to filter off. There's no simple way of seeing when you have added just enough of the solid to neutralise the acid.

items.label: text
items.text: You normally make these salts from sodium or potassium hydroxide or ammonia solution, but you can also use the carbonates. Fortunately, the solutions of all these are alkaline. That means you can find out when you have a neutral solution by using an indicator.

items.label: text
items.text: The method of finding out exactly how much of two solutions you need for them to neutralise each other is called titration (see Chapter 16). You carry out a titration using an indicator to tell you when you have added exactly enough of the acid to neutralise the alkali. items.label: list_item
items.text: 25 cm³ of sodium hydroxide solution is transferred to a conical flask using a pipette, and a few drops of methyl orange are added as the indicator.

items.label: list_item
items.text: Dilute sulfuric acid is run in from the burette until the indicator just turns from yellow to orange.

items.label: list_item
items.text: The volume of acid needed is noted, and the same volumes of acid and alkali are mixed together in a clean flask without any indicator.

items.text: The crystals are finally separated from any remaining solution by filtration (or the remaining solution can be poured away).
